clue.text: Spiv with detailed plan, lout recalled

indicators.note: de-tailed means having its tail, the final letter, cut off

parts.note: a plan is an idea

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for lout is read backwards

parts.note: a lout is a yob, British slang for a hooligan

explanation.surface: A shady dealer arrives with an elaborate scheme while some thug is summoned back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'elaborate' but means losing the tail: IDEA becomes IDE. A SPIV is a British flashy small-time black-marketeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a flashy petty crook living on his wits.

clue.text: Young woman crossing river shows strain

indicators.note: the girl's word goes across, so straddles, the river's letter

parts.note: wench is an old word for a young woman

explanation.surface: A girl wading over a river looks the worse for the effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to strain a muscle or joint is to twist it painfully.

clue.text: Arrest Greek character during row

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a row is a noisy din
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Police seize a Greek in the middle of a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to arrest a suspect is to hold or keep them in custody.

clue.text: British want to protect the blighter

parts.note: want in the sense of need or shortage is lack
to protect is to guard

explanation.surface: Britain is reluctant to shield the scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both are dated British words for a contemptible rogue or scoundrel.

clue.text: Country's desire to have Middle East involved

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up in, so the desire word holds the region's letters

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A nation wants a say in Middle Eastern affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a country at the southern tip of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Publisher entertained by very French companies

indicators.note: entertained by means received within, so the publisher sits inside

parts.note: tres is French for very
OUP is Oxford University Press

explanation.surface: A publisher is lavishly hosted by French firms.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: theatrical companies are groups of touring performers.

clue.text: Fit to bust, tart somehow gets revenge

indicators.note: bust means broken apart, so the letters of fit to are smashed and reassembled
somehow means in some unknown way, signalling that the letters of tart are reworked

explanation.surface: Furious enough to explode, a jilted woman finds some way to get even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit to bust' reads as an idiom of fury, but 'bust' rearranges FIT TO into TITFO, and 'somehow' rearranges TART into RTAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for retaliation in kind: paying back a blow with an equal blow.

clue.text: Fail to include old Cambridge seat of learning

parts.note: MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: Someone forgets to mention the ancient English university town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge' points to England, but it is the Cambridge in Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to leave something out or skip it.

clue.text: Easy to carry — piano or desk?

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a desk is a kind of table to work at

explanation.surface: Which is easier to move, a piano or a desk?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something light enough to be carried about.

clue.text: Vessel more willingly boarded by companion

indicators.note: boarded by means having someone climb aboard, so the companion's letters go inside

parts.note: I would sooner means I would more willingly
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A ship happily welcomes a friend on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a fore-and-aft rigged sailing ship with two or more masts.

clue.text: Further bit player

definitions.meaning: further means additional, more on top
a bit player is a film actor in a non-speaking crowd part

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: something additional, and a background actor in a film crowd.

clue.text: Head of family, perhaps, could make protest about curtailed hearing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the protest word goes round the rest

parts.note: a protest is a march

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail, the last letter, cut

parts.note: a hearing in court is a trial

explanation.surface: A family elder threatens to demonstrate over a court case cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a woman who rules a family, signalled by 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Yellow River associated with unknown disease

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, which is chicken
the Po is the great river of northern Italy
X is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mysterious illness is linked to a jaundiced river.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: varicella, the itchy spotty childhood illness.

clue.text: Oscar after Henry's ring

indicators.note: after places the Oscar letter behind the Henry name

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Oscar statuette follows Henry's wedding band.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a circle of light, such as the ring round a saint's head.

clue.text: Used to agree with husband too

parts.note: to second a motion is to agree with and support it
and means also or too

explanation.surface: Someone is in the habit of backing their husband as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: pre-owned goods that were not bought new.

clue.text: Coming from the sea, unexpectedly

definitions.meaning: the blue is a poetic name for the sea, so this is emerging from it

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: literally emerging from the sea or sky, and an idiom for something arriving without warning.

clue.text: Duty of Bede, I suspect, in ordinary northern church

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the other three abbreviations

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful or dodgy, signalling the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: The Venerable Bede's sense of duty in a northern church is ordinary, one suspects.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venerable Bede was a Northumbrian monk, so the northern church fits the surface; 'suspect' is the anagram signal for BEDE plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: obedience is dutiful compliance, as owed by a monk to his order.

clue.text: Man, humorist in play

parts.note: a king is a man, a piece in chess
Edward Lear was the Victorian writer of nonsense verse

explanation.surface: A man who is a comedian performs in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Shakespeare's tragedy about an old monarch and his three daughters.

clue.text: Very clean, unlike a leopard?

definitions.meaning: a leopard has spots, so the opposite is without spots

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: immaculately clean, and literally having no markings, unlike the big cat.

clue.text: Tense, working to seal one fault

indicators.note: to seal means to close around, so the tense and working words together enclose the one

parts.note: the imperfect is a grammatical tense for ongoing past action
on means working, as a machine that is on
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nervous person at work hides a single flaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective meaning nervous, but it is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a flaw or defect in something.

clue.text: Fungal growth, slight on endless sheep

parts.note: slight means mild or not severe

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A mould has crept slightly over a sheep with no end in sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a whitish mould that coats plants and damp surfaces.

clue.text: One taking a lot of interest in ancient city, certain to be impressed

definitions.text: One taking a lot of interest

indicators.note: impressed means pressed into, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A keen visitor to an old city is sure to be wowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of interest' reads as enthusiasm, but means charging excessive interest on loans.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a moneylender charging extortionate interest rates.

clue.text: Attendance good at start of event

indicators.note: start of means take only the opening letter

explanation.surface: A good turnout at the beginning of the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the gate is the number of spectators at a sports match.

clue.text: Writing about it, girl becomes unpredictable

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the writing word goes round it

parts.note: a person's hand is their handwriting
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A girl's letters about something turn erratic.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: random, sometimes succeeding and sometimes not.

clue.text: A quarrel about right marker

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the quarrel word goes round the letter

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: An argument erupts over the correct signpost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' is also an old word for a crossbow bolt, a nice echo of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a pointing sign that marks a direction.

clue.text: Box blows over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for blows is read backwards

parts.note: raps are sharp blows or knocks

explanation.surface: A boxer's punches are finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to box in practice, exchanging punches with a partner.

clue.text: Watch first batsman? Quite something

parts.note: to eye is to watch
in cricket the opener is one of the first two batsmen in

explanation.surface: Seeing the leading cricketer bat is quite a spectacle.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a revelation, something surprising or remarkable.

clue.text: Tree, thinner on top having been pollarded

indicators.note: pollarding a tree cuts off its top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a man thinner on top is balder

explanation.surface: A tree is sparser at the crown after its branches were lopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thinner on top' looks like a tree's crown but means going bald.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Hold back substitute

definitions.meaning: to keep something back for later
a replacement player kept on the bench

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to keep back for future use, and a stand-in team player.

clue.text: Ladies' group — function we run for a man on his own, perhaps

definitions.text: a man on his own, perhaps

parts.note: the WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation
a do is a party or function
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: The Women's Institute holds a social for a lonely man.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a man whose wife has died, now alone, as 'perhaps' warns.
